# alta_vlan (Resource)

One network, written through the Alta cloud so the portal shows it.

Networks that exist in the portal and not in Terraform are left alone: this resource owns its own VLAN and nothing else. The change is applied as one gated, commit-confirmed transaction — a single push to the router, rolled back automatically unless the health probes pass.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A network belongs to the site, so it takes the provider's site_id and names no device.
resource "alta_vlan" "lab" {
  vlan_id = 40

  name         = "Lab"
  router_ip    = "198.18.40.1/24"
  pool_size    = 243
  reserved_ips = 10
  domain_name  = "lan"
  dns_servers  = ["192.0.2.10", "192.0.2.1"]
}

# Describe the network once. Everything that follows from it — the subnet its hosts sit
# in, the router's own name for it, the number a port tags — is derived rather than
# written out a second time and kept in step by hand.
resource "alta_dhcp_reservation" "printer" {
  mac = "02:00:00:aa:bb:cc"
  ip  = cidrhost(alta_vlan.lab.subnet, 40)
}

resource "alta_static_route" "lab_return" {
  name      = "Lab return path"
  type      = "interface"
  network   = "198.18.41.0/24"
  interface = alta_vlan.lab.network # "lan_40"
}

resource "alta_switch_port" "lab_uplink" {
  port         = 4
  tagged_vlans = [alta_vlan.lab.vlan_id]
}

# Adopt a network the portal already has by its number:
#
#   terraform import alta_vlan.lab 40
#
# Name the site in the import id only for a site other than the provider's:
#
#   terraform import alta_vlan.lab "$SITE_ID/40"
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `vlan_id` (Number) VLAN number. Changing it is a different network, so the old one is removed and the new one created.

### Optional

- `dhcp` (Boolean) Serve DHCP on this network.
- `dns_servers` (List of String) DNS servers handed out by DHCP, in order.
- `domain_name` (String) DHCP domain name.
- `isolation` (Boolean) Isolate clients from each other.
- `mdns` (Boolean) Repeat mDNS into this network.
- `name` (String) Name shown in the portal.
- `pool_size` (Number) DHCP pool size.
- `reserved_ips` (Number) Addresses at the start of the subnet kept out of the pool.
- `router_ip` (String) Router address and prefix, e.g. `203.0.113.1/24`.
- `site_id` (String) Alta site. Defaults to the provider's `site_id`.

### Read-Only

- `gateway` (String) The router's address on this network, without the prefix.
- `id` (String) The VLAN number, as a string.
- `interface` (String) The bridge the router puts this network on.
- `network` (String) The router's own name for this network, as a firewall zone lists it and an interface route names it. Pass it to `alta_static_route.interface` rather than writing it out.
- `subnet` (String) The network in CIDR form, so hosts on it can be derived in one place: `cidrhost(alta_vlan.home.subnet, 40)`.
